data.heading: Trying meditation for the first time
data.body:
Many people come to [Temple Name] curious about meditation but unsure where to start. Here's what to expect at your first session.

When you arrive, someone will welcome you and show you where to leave your shoes. You can sit on a cushion or a chair, whichever is more comfortable. There's no right way to look.

The session usually begins with a short introduction. Then we sit quietly together for a period of meditation. [Describe the length and the instructions given in your tradition.]

Your mind will wander. That's completely normal, and it happens to everyone. When you notice it, gently come back. That noticing is part of the practice.

Some sessions include walking meditation or chanting. If you're not sure what to do, simply follow along or sit quietly.

Afterwards, there's often tea and a chance to ask questions. Teachers and regular members are happy to help.

There's no need to sign up or bring anything. Just come along to one of our beginner sessions.

data.heading: What happens at a dharma talk
data.body:
A dharma talk is a teaching on Buddhist practice and how it relates to everyday life. At [Temple Name], talks are given by [Teacher Name / our teachers] at our [Day] evening sessions.

Talks usually follow a period of meditation. The speaker may explore a teaching from our tradition, share reflections on practice, or talk about how to meet daily challenges with more awareness and kindness.

You don't need any background to listen. Talks are given in plain language, and newcomers are always welcome.

There is often time for questions or discussion afterwards. It's fine to simply listen.

Talks are offered freely. If a talk raises questions for you, you're welcome to speak with [Teacher Name] after the session or at another time.

If you can't join in person, [explain whether talks are recorded or streamed and where to find them].

We hope you'll come and listen. Check the schedule for upcoming talks.
